title: Block: Group By a Key
oneLiner: Group words by their first letter (ignoring case), keeping groups in the order their key first appeared.
keyTakeaway: Grouping is a map from key to list: look the key up, start an empty list the first time, append. Group Anagrams is this block with a different key.
explanation:
Given non-empty words, return lists of words grouped by first letter, ignoring case. Groups come in the order their letter first appeared, and words keep their input order inside a group. ["apple", "Bob", "avocado"] gives [["apple", "avocado"], ["Bob"]].

Work out the key for each word (its first character, lowercased), fetch that key's list, creating an empty one the first time, and append. Python dicts keep insertion order, so list(groups.values()) is already in first-appearance order. In C#, keep a separate list of keys in the order you created them rather than relying on Dictionary enumeration order.

gotchas: Creating a new list for every word instead of once per key, which keeps only the last word of each group.

complexity.note: One pass over the n words with O(1) average map work each; the groups hold every word once.
